query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a surface aluminization treatment to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a thin, adherent Al2O3 scale that greatly improves its oxygen resistance during long‐term high‐temperature exposure without degrading its mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr showing 8–16% room‐temperature tensile ductility and yield strengths of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C but with poor oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Subject the cast alloy’s surface to a pack cementation aluminization treatment (for example, by embedding in an Al-rich powder mixture) at roughly 900 °C for several hours followed by a controlled oxidation step to develop a continuous Al2O3 layer.
generation.conditions: Exposure tests performed at 1000 °C in air for a prolonged duration (e.g., 100 hours) with mechanical loading conditions comparable to those of the untreated alloy (strain rates between 10⁻⁴ and 10⁻² s⁻¹ and static high-temperature stress within the 163–530 MPa range).
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous, adherent, and dense Al2O3 (alumina) scale formed on the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: The aluminization process enriches the alloy’s surface with aluminum. When exposed to high-temperature oxidative conditions, the aluminum reacts to form a protective Al2O3 scale that impedes oxygen diffusion into the bulk. This barrier minimizes internal oxidation and microstructural degradation while the bulk composition—and thus its yield strength and ductility—remains essentially unaltered.
generation.predicted_outcome: After treatment and exposure at 1000 °C, the treated alloy will show a markedly lower oxide mass gain and thinner, more protective oxide scale compared to the untreated alloy, while maintaining mechanical performance (yield strength and ductility) similar to the as-cast condition.
generation.baseline: Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxidation resistance; prolonged high-temperature air exposure leads to significant oxidation-related degradation that can compromise its mechanical properties.
generation.boundary: The protective effect is expected under high-temperature oxidative conditions (~1000 °C for up to 100 hours). Effects under cyclic thermal/mechanical loads or over longer durations are not established by this hypothesis.
generation.uncertainty: It is uncertain how stable and adherent the Al2O3 scale will remain under extended thermal cycling or mechanical stress, and whether its formation might influence fatigue behavior.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples. Subject one group to the pack cementation aluminization treatment and leave the other untreated. Expose both groups to 1000 °C in air for 100 hours. Before and after exposure, measure mass gain, oxide scale thickness/morphology (using SEM or similar techniques), and assess mechanical properties (e.g., tensile yield strength and ductility) at room temperature and at high temperature.
measurements: Yield strength and ductility in tensile tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the aluminized samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in oxidation (i.e., their mass gain and oxide scale thickness are comparable to or worse than untreated samples) or if their mechanical properties are degraded (e.g., yield strength or ductility drops outside the accepted range) after high-temperature exposure.
